How Heat Pumps Simplify Climate Control

In essence, heat pumps are exactly what they sound like - devices that pump heat from one area to another. More specifically, they use a basic refrigeration cycle to absorb and release thermal energy in much the same way as air conditioners. The crucial difference is that heat pumps are reversible, allowing them to provide heating as well as cooling.

Even on seemingly cold days, the air in the environment contains a considerable amount of ambient heat. Heat pumps can warm your home without burning fuel by collecting and concentrating this heat energy. Not only is this process cleaner and more efficient, but it also produces gentler and more consistent warmth.
